items.name: Action Points
items.desc: Action Points (AP) represent your physical energy. AP is used to:    - Sprint (hold [Sprint] while moving)    - Power Attack ([Melee])    - Perform attacks in V.A.T.S. ([VATS] to open V.A.T.S., [PrimaryAttack] to attack)    - Steady your aim while using a scoped weapon ([SecondaryAttack] to aim, [Steady] to steady)    Sprinting and steadying your aim consume AP continually. Power Attacks and attacks in V.A.T.S. consume a set amount. Actions that consume AP are cancelled or blocked when your AP is too low.    AP will start to regenerate once it is no longer being consumed. If your AP is not regenerating, you might be carrying too much, or you might be holding down the Sprint button out of habit.    If you want to increase your Action Points or make your actions more efficient:    - Choose Agility when you level up to increase your total AP.    - Choose Endurance when you level up to reduce the amount of AP consumed from sprinting.    - Heal yourself if your torso is crippled. A crippled torso reduces how fast AP regenerates.    - Consume items that grant temporary bonuses to AP, Agility, or Endurance.    - Find other ways to increase your AP through Perks, Mutations, and other bonuses.    Your total AP is listed in the Pip-Boy on the Stat tab. When consumed, your AP displays on screen until fully recovered.

items.name: Activity & Public Events
items.desc: Activities:    Activities are public quests that everyone inside their area can participate in, and tend to require a small number of Vault dwellers to complete.    If you wander into an area with an active Activity, you'll receive a notification in the lower-right side of the screen. You'll be added to the Activity if you stay in the area. If you leave the area, you'll receive a similar notification that you'll be removed from the Activity if you don't return.    Any active Activities in the world will also appear on your Map as flashing hexagons. If you select an Activity from the Map, you can fast travel there and join the Activity. Fast Traveling to an Activity costs caps based on your distance traveled. You must not be over encumbered to fast travel to the Activity.    Enclave Activities are public quests run by the secretive Enclave. While anyone can participate in these Activities, members of the Enclave may receive additional rewards.    Everyone inside the Activity area earns rewards when it completes.    Public Events:    Public Events are public quests that everyone inside their area can participate in, and tend to require a significant number of Vault dwellers to complete.    If you wander into an area with an active Public Event, you'll receive a notification in the lower-right side of the screen. You'll be added to the Public Event if you stay in the area. If you leave the area, you'll receive a similar notification that you'll be removed from the Public Event if you don't return.    Any active Public Events in the world will also appear on your Map as flashing hexagons. If you select a Public Event from the Map, you can fast travel there and join the Public Event. Fast Traveling to a Public Event is free, but you must not be not over encumbered.    Everyone inside the Public Event area earns rewards when it completes.

items.name: Best Builds
items.desc: Best Builds allows players to Submit, Visit, and Rate submitted C.A.M.P.s.     Submitted Best Builds will be populated and shared throughout the Wasteland for all players across all Adventure Mode servers to visit and see.      Submitting Your Camp  You can Submit your C.A.M.P. through the Best Builds Submission option. This is found by opening the Paper Map, opening the 'C.A.M.P. Slots' list, and selecting the C.A.M.P. you wish to submit.    Once you have entered the Submission Window, you'll be able to take and add photos and tag your C.A.M.P. with the appropriate identifiers to make it stand out. Once you are happy with how your C.A.M.P. is represented, you can Submit your Best Build.    The Best Build submission will be added to the list of player-created Best Builds and will be populated across the Adventure Mode servers. Once populated, players will be able to visit and 'Like' your Best Build.     If you happen to make changes to your Best Build, you can easily resubmit the C.A.M.P. without losing any previously earned 'Likes'. You can resubmit your Best Build by going to the 'Manage Best Builds' option, also found within the 'C.A.M.P. Slots' list, on the Paper Map.      Visiting a Best Build  Populated Best Builds are indicated by a Blue Ribbon around Map Markers in the Paper Map and on the Compass.     These are our player-created Best Builds. You will be able to fast travel to these C.A.M.P.s the same as you would any other C.A.M.P..     While visiting, please take time to sit down, relax, and enjoy the experience the builder has in store for you. Don't delay on checking out a C.A.M.P. that piques your interest; Best Builds are refreshed every hour.      Rating a Best Build  If you find a Best Build that you appreciate, you can show your support to the builder by giving them a 'Like'. You can 'Like' a Best Build by going to the Best Build Icon on the Paper Map and selecting 'Like'.     Your 'Likes' help other players identify the best of the Best Builds.

items.name: Blueprints
items.desc: Blueprints are a way to group objects together so you can build them again all at once. You can access Blueprints by entering building mode at your C.A.M.P. or a Workshop that you own.      Creating a Blueprint  While in building mode, navigate to the Blueprints category and press [XButton] to start creating or modifying a Blueprint.    Select an object you've built by walking up to it and centering it on your screen until it becomes highlighted. Hold [Accept] to add it to the Blueprint.    Add as many objects to the Blueprint as you want. Their position and rotation relevant to each other will all be stored in the Blueprint.    Press [RTrigger] to create the Blueprint.       Select Structure Option  The Select Structure option ([LShoulder]) will select every object that is attached to the selected object. Walls are typically attached to foundations and other walls, creating a single structure that the Blueprint can select.      Grow Selection Option  The Grow Selection option ([RShoulder]) will attempt to select any objects that are near the selected objects.

items.name: Bounty Hunting
items.desc: The Ghoul needs your help to track down targets across Burning Springs.    Grunt Hunts  You may start a Grunt Hunt at any time for free.  To begin your mission, interact with the stack of contracts at the Last Resort saloon in Highway Town. After getting your target, head to the location specified in your objective and prepare to fight! Killing the target will give you rewards, and you can loot their body for additional items. After all, they won't be needing them, will they?    Head Hunts  After completing a few Grunt Hunts, you might receive a Wanted Poster for a powerful Head Hunt target.  If you're not chosen, but you still think you're strong enough, Wanted Posters can also be purchased from the Ghoul. After obtaining a poster, pin it on the board outside the saloon to inform others that you have started a hunt.    Your contract will tell you where the target is located. Head Hunts are tough and will often have back-up, so use the flare to alert other Vault Dwellers of their location. Only one Head Hunt can be active at a time, so band together to take down those dastardly outlaws before they can get away.  A successful Head Hunt will give you glory... and a great payout.   Happy hunting!

items.name: Bullet Storm
items.desc: With the Bullet Storm Perk equipped you gain a stacking buff from spending ammo. All stacks are lost when you reload or change weapons. The count of ammo spent carries over between reloads. Weapons that fire multiple projectiles grant bonus ammo spent. Other Perks and items can add and enhance the effects of Bullet Storm.

items.name: C.A.M.P.
items.desc: The C.A.M.P. (Construction and Assembly Mobile Platform) allows you to build your own corner of Appalachia in any way you see fit.     Setting up C.A.M.P.   [Pipboy] then [LShoulder] - Open your Pip-Boy then set your C.A.M.P.    The C.A.M.P. will appear in front of you, highlighted in either blue or red. If the highlight is blue,     [Activate] - Place your C.A.M.P.    If the highlight is red, the C.A.M.P. cannot be placed here. It might be too close to an existing location or the ground might not be flat enough. Move around until you find a position where the C.A.M.P. turns blue.    Benefits of the C.A.M.P.  Your C.A.M.P. appears on your map as an icon of your choice. Fast traveling to your C.A.M.P. is always free, regardless of how far away it is from you.    One of the most important items you can build at your C.A.M.P. is the Stash Box. A Stash Box can store a large amount of items and is secure against other Players. Only you can see and access your stash.    Moving your C.A.M.P.   You can move your C.A.M.P. to a new location.    [Pipboy] then [LShoulder] - Open your Pip-Boy then move your C.A.M.P.    When you move your C.A.M.P., anything you built at your old site is packed up and placed in the Stored category in the building mode menu.    When you log out from the game, your C.A.M.P. is packed up. When you log back on, the game will try to set up your C.A.M.P. the way you left it.

items.name: C.A.M.P. - Create Buildings
items.desc: A building starts with a Foundation. Go to C.A.M.P. Pieces then Foundations category and select one of the Foundations to build. Once you've built a Foundation, you can attach more Foundations to it, increasing the size of your flooring.    You can then attach Walls, Roofs, Stairs, and Doors to the Foundation pieces to create an entire building.    If you want to create buildings with multiple stories, you'll first need to attach a set of Stairs to your Foundation. Then, go to the Floor category and select one of the Floor pieces, then attach them to the top of your stairs to start your second story.

items.name: C.A.M.P. - Relaxed Build Rules
items.desc: Relaxed build rules are automatically toggled on in Settings/Game/Workshop Building Rules.    With relaxed build rules, all items are allowed to float, intersect with each other, and be unsupported. There are three different placement modes that players can toggle between.    [Remove] - Toggle object placement modes in Build mode    In Snap mode, the item will consider collisions and try to auto-snap to other items.     In Collision mode, this item will not try to auto-snap but will still consider collisions.     In Free mode, no collision and no snapping.

items.name: C.A.M.P. Pets
items.desc: Bring a little life to your C.A.M.P. with your very own C.A.M.P. pet!  C.A.M.P. Pets are permanent dwellers at your personal C.A.M.P. that you can interact with while they generate treasures for you.    Once unlocked, C.A.M.P. Pets will have a unique workshop item that can be built at your C.A.M.P. Building this item summons your new C.A.M.P. pet, allowing you to interact with them, giving your C.A.M.P. Pet the ability to interact with your C.A.M.P., and starting the C.A.M.P. pet's treasure finding ability.    C.A.M.P. Pets have unique workshop items that only they can interact with. These items can be found in your workshop menu. Once placed in your C.A.M.P., your active C.A.M.P. Pet will intermittently use the objects, so keep an eye on them.    While active in your C.A.M.P., your C.A.M.P. Pet will find small treasures to give you as a sign of affection. These treasures can be found while you are away from your C.A.M.P. and your C.A.M.P. pet will deliver them to you once you return. So, remember to head back home from time to time to see what your little friend has found!    To remove your C.A.M.P. Pet, scrap or store the C.A.M.P. pet's workshop object and that C.A.M.P. pet will leave your C.A.M.P. until you choose to rebuild it.    You can only have one C.A.M.P. Pet at your C.A.M.P. at a time, so choose the one that best fits your C.A.M.P.!

items.name: C.A.M.P. Titles
items.desc: C.A.M.P. Titles allow you to customize the display name for yourC.A.M.P. with both a Prefix and Suffix. C.A.M.P. Titles display at the bottom of the C.A.M.P. name.      Changing your C.A.M.P. name.  Title is done on the Map. Enter the C.A.M.P. widget to select C.A.M.P.  Title.    C.A.M.P. Titles can be unlocked numerous ways including, but not limited to, Seasons, Recipe Books, and by completing some quests and challenges.

items.name: Caravans
items.desc: Caravans  Escort and defend Brahmin on the perilous Skyline Drive! Travel along one of several predetermined routes, defend cargo from vicious enemies, and deposit it into a box at the end of its path to receive a substantial reward.    Setting Up a Caravan  To begin running caravans, visit Stony Man Lookout at level 20 (minimum) and follow the clues to Milepost Zero. Marley will need your help with deliveries. After talking to her and starting a new mission, open the paper map and select your caravan. This can be identified by a Brahmin head icon and your character's name. Clicking it will transport you to the Brahmin, and you can begin your new job.  You may run one small caravan for free each hour. If you'd like to run more caravans after your first free one, talk to Marley. She will charge you a gradually decreasing fee and get you set up with a new caravan route.    Supplies  Safely delivering your cargo will award you a new currency known as Supplies, as well as various miscellaneous items. Your Supply reward will vary depending on cargo size, which can be adjusted by talking to Marley, but be warned: bigger cargo shipments will lead to a more difficult challenge on the road.  Supplies can be used to upgrade Milepost Zero in many exciting ways. Hire new employees, promote them, or talk to them when they arrive at your base to purchase various services.    Multiple Caravans  Embark on your own caravan adventure, or join friends to earn Supplies together. A maximum of three caravans can be running on the map at once, but one player can only own one caravan. Any caravans that are already on the road can be seen by opening the paper map.

items.name: Carry Weight
items.desc: Carry Weight represents how much you can haul in your inventory before it starts to slow you down. The more Strength you have, the more you can carry.    Each item you pick up has a Weight value. If the total Weight of all your items exceeds your Carry Weight, you start to suffer penalties:    - You will not be able to Fast Travel.    - Your Action Points (AP) will drain when you move and you won't be able to Sprint. AP will regenerate whenever you stand still.    - When you run out of AP, you will be forced to move at walking speed. You can move at full speed again when you recover enough AP.    The fastest way to reduce your inventory Weight is to drop items.    To drop an item, press [Pipboy] to enter the Pip-Boy and navigate to the Items tab with [LTrigger]/[RTrigger].  Highlight the item(s) you wish to drop using [LeftStick] and press [XButton].    Items you drop will appear in the world inside a Paper Bag. Other players can loot this bag, and the bag will disappear over time.    If you want to increase your Carry Weight or reduce the Weight of items:    - Choose Strength when you level up to increase your total Carry Weight.    - Wear a suit of Power Armor. The suit will increase your Strength as long as you're in it.    - Equip Perks like Thru-Hiker or Packin' Light to reduce the Weight of certain items.    - Consume items that temporarily raise Strength, like Buffout.    - Store excess items in a secure container, like your Stash Box.

items.name: Checkpoints
items.desc: Checkpoint notifications are sent whenever a Quest is saving your progress.    When you log out, your Quests will restart at the last Checkpoint.    Certain Quests, such as Events and Daily Quests, are never saved and will always go away if you log out before completing them.

items.name: Chems
items.desc: Chems are consumable items that grant temporary bonuses. You can find Chems in your Pip-Boy under Item -> Aid.    While Chems can be very powerful, there are drawbacks:    - Chems can inflict Thirst and Hunger to Humans.    - Chems carry a risk of Addiction when used.    - Chems sometimes have penalties alongside their bonuses.    - Only one Chem can be active at a time. If you take a new Chem before the old one expires, the effects of the old Chem immediately end. You'll still suffer any Thirst, Hunger, or Addiction checks from the old Chem.    You can see the effects of your current Chem by opening your Pip-Boy and going to Stat -> Effects.      Addiction  If you have an Addiction to a Chem, you'll suffer Withdrawal penalties when you don't take the Chem periodically.    To cure Addiction completely, you need to take Addictol, a rare medicine.    You can see the effects of any Withdrawal penalties you have by opening your Pip-Boy and going to Status -> Effects.    Feral  Chems will be restoring Feral to Ghoul Characters.

items.name: Compass
items.desc: The Compass is displayed at the bottom of your screen and gives you important information about your environment.    Along with the current direction you're heading, any undiscovered locations of interest will appear on your compass in outline. The closer you get to a location, the larger its icon will become. Once you've discovered a location, its icon will fill.     Nearby enemies are also displayed on the compass. How far away an enemy can be before appearing on your compass is determined by your Perception attribute. The better your Perception, the further away you'll be able to spot enemies.    Detected enemies will appear as red dots on the compass. If the enemy is above or below you, an arrow will appear on their dot to indicate their direction.    Other players will appear on the compass as yellow dots. Teammates will appear as gold dots, and Hostile players will appear as red dots.    Quest targets for your active quests will appear on your compass as yellow diamonds. Like enemies, if your target is above or below you, an arrow will appear on the diamond to indicate its direction.    Area quest targets appear on your compass as yellow circles. You can see the entire area the target points to by opening your Map [Map]. When you enter the area, the compass will flash.

items.name: Crafting
items.desc: Crafting items is done by going to the appropriate workbench/station:    - Armor Workbench: for Armor, Armor Mods, Backpacks, CAMP Pet Clothing, Underarmor, and general Clothing    - Chemistry Station: for Chems and ingredients like Gunpowder or smelted ore    - Cooking Station: for Food, Drinks, and Herbal Remedies    - Power Armor Station: for Power Armor pieces and Power Armor Mods    - Tinker's Workbench: for Ammo, Flamer Fuel, Grenades, Mines, Chests, Fishing, Gifts, Legendary Mods, Quest Items, and Souvenirs    - Weapons Workbench: for Guns, Melee Weapons, and Weapon Mods      Components  Crafting an item consumes Components, which are found primarily in Junk items. An old Lantern you find might contain Glass and Steel, for example.    Components are automatically consumed when you craft, destroying the item that held the Components. Anything not used will be refunded to you as raw Components.    If you want to see which Components an item has, Open the Pip-Boy and go to the Items category to see what you're currently carrying. Select an item, and any Components it has will appear next to the description.      Tagging Components for Search  When you select an item to craft, Components that you don't have are grayed out. If you press [R3], it will tag the missing Components for search. The Components will have a magnifying glass icon next to them. Whenever you are searching a container, any item that has a Component you have tagged will have the magnifying glass icon next to it.      Storing Junk Items  You can store your Junk items quickly using the Stash Box. Approach a Stash Box and press [XButton] to open the Transfer Menu, then [YButton] to Store All Junk.    Any items stored in the Stash Box are available when you're crafting items at a workbench or station.      Scrapping Junk Items  You can scrap your Junk items at any crafting station or workbench. Approach the workbench and press [XButton] to open the Scrap Items Menu, then [YButton] to Scrap All Junk.    When you scrap Junk items, you'll receive all the crafting components from them. Components weigh significantly less, so scrapping your Junk items whenever you find a crafting workbench in the world will help you stay under your Carry Weight.      Item Condition  Some items, like weapons and armor, degrade as they're used. This is tracked in the Condition bar. When the Condition bar is empty, the item will break.    You can view an item's current Condition by opening the Pip-Boy, going to the Items category, and selecting the specific item.    When you craft an item, the starting Condition of the item is based on your Intelligence.    When you find an item in the world, the starting Condition of the item is based on your Luck.      Repairing Items  Repairs to an item can be made at the same workbench/station where you craft the item. Walk up to the workbench and press [YButton] to enter the Modify/Repair menu. If you're already using the workbench, you can switch between the Modify/Repair menu and the Crafting menu by hitting [XButton].      Modifications  Armor, Weapons, and Power Armor can all be enhanced with Mods. Walk up to the workbench and press [YButton] to enter the Modify/Repair menu. If you're already using the workbench, you can switch between the Modify/Repair menu and the Crafting menu by hitting [XButton].    Mods occupy a slot on the item, such as the barrel, grip, or sights. While only one Mod can be installed in each slot, you can craft new Mods to replace any existing Mod.      Recipes/Plans  Recipes and Plans allow you to craft new items. When you pick up a Recipe or Plan, open your Pip-Boy [Pipboy] and go to Item -> Notes, then activate the Recipe or Plan in order to learn from it. The Recipe or Plan will be consumed in the process.    If you find another copy of the Recipe or Plan, activating it again will do nothing, but it can be traded or sold.      Other Ways of Learning New Crafting Items  You can also learn new crafting options when you pick up certain items. The first time you pick up a new raw meat or plant ingredient, for example, you will learn a basic cooking recipe for it. Picking up Gunpowder will teach you how to make more at the Chemistry Station. There are even new decoration options for your C.A.M.P. that you can unlock by picking up signs and other household objects.    Scrapping items, particularly new Weapons, Armor, and Mods that you find while exploring, can also unlock the ability to craft them yourself. Make sure you don't need the item before you scrap it! Try scrapping a piece of Wood Armor or a Pipe Gun Mod you aren't using and see if you've learned how to make it yourself.

items.name: Damage - Cryo
items.desc: Represented by a Snowflake icon    Cryo damage can be found in advanced weaponry such as the Cryolator as well as specialized modifications for certain weapons.    - Cryo damage is commonly paired with a Slow effect which reduces the speed of the affected target for a short period of time.    Smaller and lightly-armored targets tend to be less resistant to Cryo   damage.  Creatures with thick fur are resistant to Cryo damage.  Robots and other inorganic targets are strongly resistant to Cryo damage.

items.name: Damage - Energy
items.desc: Represented by a Lightning Bolt icon    Energy damage is most frequently dealt by Laser and Plasma Weapons, as well as attacks which utilize electricity.  It's also featured in extraterrestrial and otherworldly attacks.    Energy damage is most effective against electronic and metallic enemies such as Robots and Turrets.

items.name: Damage - Fire
items.desc: Represented by a Flame icon    Fire damage can be found from specialized weapons like Flamers and modified weapons which feature incendiary rounds, jets of flame, or heating elements.  Burning objects throughout Appalachia and even some creatures can also deal Fire damage.    - Fire damage is typically paired with a Damage over Time effect which deals additional damage over a short period of time.    Fire damage is effective against lightly-armored targets and hostile wildlife.  Hardened targets such as Robots and fortified defenses are often resistant to fire.

items.name: Damage - Physical
items.desc: Represented by a Shield icon    Physical damage typically occurs from bullets, blunt and sharp melee weapons, and the impact force of most explosions.  Physical damage is the most common form of damage in Appalachia and is reasonably effective against most targets.    Physical damage is most commonly resisted by armored targets such as Robots and Turrets, humans wearing Power Armor, or large creatures with thick hides.

items.name: Damage - Poison
items.desc: Represented by a Droplet icon    Poison damage can be dealt by certain plants and animals, especially Insects and mutated creatures, as well as weapons employed by humans for biological warfare.  Corrosive and acidic substances can also deal Poison damage.    - Poison damage is typically paired with a Damage over Time effect which deals additional damage over a long period of time.    Poison damage is most effective against lightly-armored organic targets.  Inorganic enemies such as Robots are often immune to Poison damage.

items.name: Damage - Radiation
items.desc: Represented by a Radiation icon    Radiation damage is common in areas that are highly irradiated such as Nuke Zones and storage facilities for nuclear waste.  Some weapons deal Radiation damage such as the Gamma Gun, and Glowing or otherwise mutated enemies may also emit Radiation either passively or when they attack.    - See the "Radiation" Help section for more information    Power Armor, certain consumable items like Rad-X, and Hazmat Suits provide high resistance to Radiation damage.    Radiation damage is most effective against lightly-armored organic targets.  Mutated and irradiated creatures can be highly resistant or even immune to Radiation damage.

items.name: Damage over Time
items.desc: Some attacks deal Damage over Time (DoT), meaning the target will continue to lose additional health after the attack impacts the target.  These effects wear off over time and can be resisted by armor, perks, or other effects that reduce damage or provide resistances to the damage type being dealt by the Damage over Time effect.    - Damage over Time effects are represented by a triangular icon under enemy health bars which will indicate the remaining duration for the effect.

items.name: Damage Reflection
items.desc: Some items and abilities may allow damage to be Reflected. This damage receives bonuses from having a higher armor rating, but is not affected by Perks or other damage modifiers.

items.name: Damage Types
items.desc: There are six damage types: Physical, Energy, Radiation, Fire, Cryo, and Poison.      The higher a target's Resistance against a given damage type, the less damage they'll take from that attack. If you have at least 10 Perception, you can view your target's Resistances when you use V.A.T.S.    - See each type's respective Help section for more detailed information    You can view the Damage Type(s) of your weapons by opening the Pip-Boy [Pipboy] and going to Item -> Weapons.    Similarly, the Damage Resistance values of your armor are viewable from Item -> Armor. You can view your total Damage Resistance values by going to Stat -> Status.

items.name: Damaged Limbs
items.desc: Your limbs, head, and torso can take damage during combat. If they take too much damage, they'll become crippled.     Crippled limbs inflict the following penalties:     - Arms - it will be harder to aim your weapon    - Legs - you will move at a reduced speed    - Torso - your Action Points will recover slower    - Head - your vision and hearing will become distorted    To restore crippled limbs, use a Stimpak. This will restore health to all your damaged limbs.    You can view the current condition of your limbs by opening the Pip-Boy and going to Stat -> Status. The Vault Boy in the center of the Status screen will display any currently crippled limbs. The small bars surrounding the Vault Boy represent the current health of each of your limbs.

items.name: Death
items.desc: Death occurs whenever your Health drops to zero.    Reviving and Respawning  You will drop to the ground and a timer will begin. If another player runs up and revives you before the timer runs out, you will stand back up. Otherwise, you will need to respawn when the timer runs out or if you press the Give Up button.    When you respawn, you will need to pick a location on the Map. Locations far away from you will cost Caps to respawn there, but you will always be able to respawn at a Teammate, Friend, your C.A.M.P., Foundation, Fort Atlas, The Crater, The Rose Room, The Rusty Pick, The Whitespring Resort, Dark Hollow Manor, Radiant Hills, Highway Town, Fisherman's Rest or Vault 76 for free.    The location of your last death will appear on your Map and the Compass as a skull and crossbones icon.      Dropped Loot  After you respawn, any Junk Items in your Inventory will be dropped where you died inside a Paper Bag.    You will receive a Miscellaneous Objective pointing to your dropped loot. If nothing was dropped, or you died in a location that is no longer available, you will not receive an objective as there is nothing to retrieve.    Any other Player can grab what you dropped when you die. Your dropped loot can also go away if you log out before retrieving it.

items.name: Deflect
items.desc: Deflect grants a chance to reduce incoming damage from a ranged attack by 50% and reflect 100% of the damage back to the attacker. Deflect chance receives a 50% bonus while wearing 5 pieces of heavy armor or while in Power Armor. While in Power Armor, the amount of damage reflected is doubled too. Explosions cannot be deflected. Bonuses to Reflected Damage also apply to Deflected attacks.

items.name: Dirty Laundry
items.desc: While exploring Burning Springs, you might spot an Abraxodyne briefcase. Pick it up to get started with the Dirty Laundry quest. Alternatively, go to the Abraxodyne Chemical Legal Office in Athens and talk to Bodhi.    After speaking to Bodhi and listening to his story, you will be tasked with collecting more briefcases scattered around the region. After collecting enough, your objective will prompt you to return to Bodhi to decrypt the information locked in each briefcase, before you are sent out again to retrieve more. He may also ask you to find caches, which store multiple briefcases.     You can track how many briefcases you've found in the Challenge Menu.

items.name: Disease
items.desc: Diseases are temporary negative effects that can afflict you after you reach Level 5. You have a chance to catch a Disease when you do any of the following:    - Sleep in a bed that's on the ground.    - Get hit in melee by a Diseased enemy.    - Drink Dirty Water.    - Move through environmental hazards.    - Eat raw food.    - Swim in dirty water.    - Get hit by a trap.    - Move through an area that has bad weather.    The chance to catch a Disease is based on your Endurance. The higher your Endurance, the lower the chance you'll catch any Disease.    You can prevent catching a Disease entirely by:    - Only sleeping in beds that have a frame.    - Avoid getting close to Diseased enemies, so they can't hit you.    - Boiling Dirty Water at a Cooking Station before drinking it.    - Wearing a Hazmat Suit or Gas Mask before moving through environmental hazards.    - Cooking raw food at a Cooking Station before eating it.    - Wearing a Hazmat Suit or Gas Mask before swimming through water.    - Watching out for traps and disarm them before they spring.    - Wearing a Hazmat Suit or Gas Mask if you're outside in bad weather.    If you've caught a Disease, you can open your Pip-Boy [Pipboy] and go to Stat -> Effects to see more information on the penalties you'll be under until the Disease is cured.    Disease Cures and Antibiotics will remove one of the Diseases you're suffering from. Diseases will also expire on their own, given enough time.

items.name: Disguises (Ghoul)
items.desc: Disguises allow ghouls to interact with factions that are hostile to ghouls as if they were human.    Quests involved with factions hostile to ghouls will be blocked until the player is in a disguise.    You can interact with Jaye Vo within the Missile Silo shelter found in Radiant Hills to be granted a Disguise.    They will be located in the Apparel Section of your Pip-Boy.    Disguises, however, have a drawback:    - Cannot Unequip naturally.    You can remove Disguises by interacting with Jaye Vo again.

items.name: Emotes
items.desc: Emotes allow you to communicate with other players.    Press [QuickkeyDown] to open the Emotes Menu. Select an Emote with [Look] and press [Accept] to trigger the Emote.    Your character will play an animation for the Emote and an icon will appear above your head.    Players who can't see you directly can still see the icon from the Emote, letting other players find you more easily.

items.name: Emotes
items.desc: Emotes allow you to communicate with other players.    Press [Emotes] to open the Emotes Menu. Select an Emote with the mouse wheel and then [Click] to trigger the Emote.    Your character will play an animation for the Emote and an icon will appear above your head.    Players who can't see you directly can still see the icon from the Emote, letting other players find you more easily.

items.name: Evade
items.desc: Evade provides a chance to avoid all incoming damage from direct attacks. Evade has a short cooldown based on the damage avoided and cannot happen when over encumbered or while in Power Armor. The cooldown is increased when wearing armor. Medium and Heavy armor have higher cooldown penalties.

items.name: Fast Travel
items.desc: Fast Travel allows you to quickly move to your Teammates, your Friends, your C.A.M.P., or return to any location you've previously discovered.    To Fast Travel, press [Map] to open the Map. Move the cursor to a Teammate, a Friend, your C.A.M.P., or a location, press [Accept], then select "Fast Travel."    Fast Traveling to a location costs a number of Caps based on how far away the location is from you. The further away you're traveling, the more Caps you'll need to pay.  Traveling to a Teammate, Friend, your C.A.M.P., Foundation, Fort Atlas, The Crater, The Rose Room, The Rusty Pick, The Whitespring Resort, Dark Hollow Manor, Radiant Hills, Highway Town, Fisherman's Rest or Vault 76 is always free regardless of distance.    You cannot Fast Travel while you are in combat, if you are carrying too much weight, or if you're taking any form of Health damage.

items.name: Fast Travel
items.desc: Fast Travel allows you to quickly move to your Teammates, your Friends, your C.A.M.P., or return to any location you've previously discovered.    To Fast Travel, press [Map] to open the Map. Select a Teammate, a Friend, your C.A.M.P., or a location with [Click], then select "Fast Travel."    Fast Traveling to a location costs a number of Caps based on how far away the location is from you. The further away you're traveling, the more Caps you'll need to pay. Traveling to a Teammate, Friend, your C.A.M.P., Foundation, Fort Atlas, The Crater, The Rose Room, The Rusty Pick, The Whitespring Resort, Dark Hollow Manor, Radiant Hills, Highway Town, Fisherman's Rest or Vault 76 is always free regardless of distance.    You cannot Fast Travel while you are in combat, if you are carrying too much weight, or if you're taking any form of Health damage.

items.name: Favorites
items.desc: To favorite an item, press [Pipboy] to open the Pip-Boy, and then go to Items. Select the item you'd like to favorite and press [RShoulder]. Weapons, Armor, Apparel, Food/Drink, and Aid items can all be favorited.    Press [QuickkeyUp] to access the Favorites menu. Select an item using [Look] and press [Accept] to use the item. Weapons and Armor will be equipped, while Aid items will be consumed.    You can continue to move while the Favorites menu is up. Press [Cancel] at any time to leave the menu.     To remove a favorited item from the menu, open the Pip-Boy and select the item you wish to remove, then press [RShoulder].

items.name: Favorites
items.desc: The Favorites menu is a way to quickly access items and gear.    To favorite an item, press [Pipboy] to open the Pip-Boy, and then go to Items. Select the item you'd like to favorite and press [RShoulder]. Weapons, Armor, Apparel, Food/Drink, and Aid items can all be favorited.    Move the mouse wheel to access the Favorites menu. Continue to move the wheel up or down to select an item, then [Click] to use the item. Weapons and Armor will be equipped, while Aid items will be consumed.    You can also access your favorites by using [Quickkeys]. Stimpaks are auto-assigned to [Quickkey12]. The first item you favorite is assigned to [Quickkey1], then [Quickkey2], and so on.    You can continue to move while the Favorites menu is up. Press [ForceClose] at any time to leave the menu.     To remove a favorited item from the menu, open the Pip-Boy and select the item you wish to remove, then press [RShoulder].

items.name: Feral Meter (Ghoul)
items.desc: Feral represents how much sanity you must have to maintain the sense of oneself.    The Feral meter appers in the lower-right corner of the screen, replacing the Hunger and Thirst meter. Feral is represented by a skull crack icon.  If you do not see either meter, you can open the Pip-Boy to bring them up.    You can restore Feral by consuming Chems & Perk Abilities.    The Feral meter drains over time. The meter provides bonuses and penalties depending on how full the meter is:    Feral Meter    - Above 80 percent: you gain +3 Strength,  +3 Endurance, +30 Max HP     - Above 60 percent: you gain +15 Max HP    - Above 40 percent: you lose -1 Endurance and -5 Max AP    - Above 25 percent: you lose -3 Endurance, -15 Max HP, -10 Max AP    - At 0 percent: you gain +150% Melee Damage, and lose -5 Endurance, -30 Max HP, -99 Charisma, -20 Max AP, -300% Hip-fire Gun Accuracy & Range V.A.T.S Accuracy.

items.name: Fishing
items.desc: Dive into the murky depths of Fisherman's Rest to receive a fishing rod. After obtaining your new kit, look for a prompt by the lake, or search for other large water sources across the region.    Hold [ReadyWeapon] - Activate fishing near a water source.    After finding a great spot to fish, select a bait, cast your line and prepare for a bite.    [Accept] - To cast  [QuickkeyLeft]/[QuickkeyRight] - Change bait sections  [Select] - Toggle camera views  [Cancel] - Exit    Watch the bobber carefully: it must be completely submerged before you begin retracting your rod, or your catch might get away.   You wouldn't want to be outsmarted by a fish, would you?    [Accept] - Start reeling in your fish  [Select] - Toggle camera view  [Cancel] - Exit    You've hooked a fish, now to secure your catch! Reel in the fish by keeping it within the zone, but be warned: some can be very slippery.    [QuickkeyLeft]/[QuickkeyRight] - Rotate catch zone  [LeftStick] - Move guide dot and catch zone  [Select] - Toggle camera view  [Cancel] - Exit    With skilled angling, you will be able to reel in your new aquatic acquaintance. From here, you may inspect your mighty catch, cast your line again or leave to find other exciting fishing spots.     [Accept] - Continue fishing  [Inspect] -  Inspect fish  [Select] - Toggle camera view  [Cancel] - Exit    Be sure to check your surroundings before fishing. Taking damage from enemies or the environment will force your character to stop fishing.    Test your prowess by completing challenges to unlock upgrades for your fishing rod. Improved and Superb bait attract only the rarest fish, and you'll have a hard time catching them without an upgraded rod. With such a mighty tool, who knows what you could catch?    Good luck out there, and just remember: A bad day of fishing is better than a good day of work!

items.name: Fishing - Seasonal Fish
items.desc: Seasonal fish are rare fish that appear in specific regions across Appalachia only during certain calendar months. For example, summer fish can only be caught during the months of June through September.    Processing seasonal fish at a cooking station creates special seasonal ingredients used to make powerful cooking recipes.  But remember, once the season changes, the fish will no longer be available until the season returns!    For information on which season is currently active, and where to find the fish, look for a Fishing Report note on Captain Raymond's desk at Fisherman's Rest in the Mire.

items.name: Food
items.desc: Food fills your Hunger meter (if you're human) and also restores lost Health.    However, most food in Appalachia causes radiation damage, reducing your maximum Health. Food will also turn rotten over time if it's not consumed. Uncooked food can also cause Disease.    Food prepared at a Cooking Station eliminates the chance of catching Disease, reduces radiation damage, and typically boosts how well it fills the Hunger meter and how much Health it restores.

items.name: Ghouls (Player)
items.desc: After reaching Level 50, the player unlocks a quest that can transform their Human Character into a Ghoul.    Playing as a Ghoul will introduce new mechanics related to Radiation, Disguising, and allows access to exclusive Perks and Legendary Perks for Ghouls.    Ghouls also will have the following stats applied to them:    -10 Charisma  100% Disease Resist    Select Human Perks will be disabled and unequipped.    Players may turn back their characters into Human through the main menu.    Any perks equipped that are ghoul exclusive will be locked out and unequipped.    Characters in custom worlds cannot revert back to human.

items.name: Glow (Ghoul)
items.desc: Exposure to radiation (or "rads"), causes Glow, increasing your maximum health.    The amount of Glow you've accumulated is displayed in a Green-stripped pattern on your HP bar. Your Pip-Boy also has a built-in radiation indicator on the right of its screen.    You can gain Glow by consuming tainted foods and beverages or being exposed to an irradiated environment. If your Pip-Boy's Geiger counter starts to click, it means you've entered an irradiated area.     The amount of Glow you are currently gaining will be displayed above your HP bar. If you're in Power Armor, your current rad intake will be displayed on the "Rads" dial next to your Hit Points.    You can use Glow for Perk Abilities that increase damage of your weapons, and mitigating any damage taken.    Any item or environment that removes rads will remove Glow instead.

items.name: Hacking
items.desc: Hacking lets you access Terminals locked with a password.    Locked Terminals have a difficulty level, usually between 0 and 3. A level 0 Terminal can always be hacked, but higher level Terminals will require you to equip Perks.    There are 3 Hacking Perks: Hacker, Expert Hacker, and Master Hacker. Each Perk you equip increases your Hacking Skill by 1. You will need to equip all 3 Perks to hack level 3 terminals.    To hack a terminal, approach it and press [Activate]. The terminal will display a list of potential passwords and random characters. Only one word listed is the correct password.    Move the cursor using [LeftStick] to select a word. Press [Accept] to attempt to use that word as the password.    If the guess is correct, the terminal will unlock.    If the guess is wrong, a "Likeness" number will be displayed in the corner of the terminal screen.    The Likeness number tells you how many letters, in the correct position, match the actual password. For example, if the password is "BOOK" and you guess "BACK",  the Likeness number is 2, because there's a "B" in position 1 and a "K" in position 4. But if you guess "OATS" the Likeness number is 0. Even though both "BOOK" and "OATS" contain the letter "O", the word "OATS" has an "O" in position 1, and the letter in position 1 of the actual password is "B", so it's not a match.    Use the Likeness number to narrow your search by comparing the letters and letter positions of your guess to the remaining options.    As you move your cursor through the lists of characters, keep an eye out for pairs of matching brackets (e.g., () {} <>). If a matching pair of brackets becomes highlighted, then selecting the brackets might remove a dud word or reset your number of attempts for the hack.    You have four attempts to select the right password. If you fail to find the correct entry after four attempts, you'll be locked out of the terminal for 10 seconds.    You can press [Cancel] at any time to exit the Terminal.

items.name: Hunger/Thirst
items.desc: Hunger and Thirst represent how much food or beverage you need to consume to gain bonuses.    The Hunger meter and the Thirst meter appear in the lower-right corner of the screen if you're a human. Hunger is represented by the fork and knife icon. Thirst is represented by the water drop icon. If you do not see either meter, you can open the Pip-Boy to bring them up.    The Hunger and Thirst meters drain over time. They each give out different bonuses depending on how full the meter is:    Hunger Meter  - Above 80 percent: you gain +1 Strength, +35 Max HP and +35 Disease Resistance.     - Above 60 percent: you gain +25 Max HP and +25 Disease Resistance.    - Above 40 percent: you gain +15 Max HP and +15 Disease Resistance.    - Above 20 percent: you gain +15 Max HP.        Thirst Meter  - Above 80 percent: you gain +1 Endurance, +35 AP Regen and +35 Disease Resistance.     - Above 60 percent: you gain +25 AP Regen and +25 Disease Resistance.    - Above 40 percent: you gain +15 AP Regen and +15 Disease Resistance.    - Above 20 percent: you gain +15 AP Regen.

items.name: Impairments
items.desc: An impairment is a negative status effect that can be applied to a target through weapons, Perks, and gameplay.    Damage over time impairments  - Burning  - Poison  - Bleeding  - Freezing    Other impairments  - Crippled

items.name: Infestation
items.desc: Infestations are limited-time, high-difficulty encounters that can appear without warning as you roam the wilds of Appalachia.     When a hostile faction seizes control of an area, its usual inhabitants are replaced with powerful and dangerous enemies - led by a highly-challenging faction boss that can drop Four-Star Legendary rewards when defeated.    Infestation events will only occur in outdoor locations within Appalachia, making familiar territory feel dangerous and unpredictable.    Active Infestation Zones will be shown on your map to provide an approximate location -  you'll only know the exact location when you walk right into it... as will your team mates.     Stay sharp out there - in Appalachia, no place stays safe for long.

items.name: Kill Streak
items.desc: Perks like Adrenaline offer a Kill Streak mechanic that allows you to gain temporary effects on killing enemies. When you kill an enemy your Kill Streak is increased by one and the Kill Streak timer is reset to 30 seconds. This can stack up to 10 times and additional kills continue to reset the timer.

items.name: Legendaries
items.desc: Legendary enemies will sometimes spawn in place of a standard opponent. Legendaries are tougher and can mutate as they take damage, causing them to regain health and deal increased damage or gain other, unique effects.    Defeating a Legendary enemy provides bonus XP and there is a chance a Legendary item will drop.

items.name: Legendary Crafting
items.desc: If a Weapon or Armor has a star after its name... it's Legendary!    These can be found by defeating creatures with stars in their names, otherwise known as Legendary Creatures. You can also find these being sold by players, as rewards for certain Quests or Public Events, or by creating them yourself using Legendary Modules and other resources on non-Legendary Items.    At their respective Workbenches, random Legendary Mods can be added to Armor, Power Armor and Weapons. Items with lower star values can also have additional Mods added to them without disrupting the existing Mods.    If you want to further customize your Legendary Weapon, you can swap out any of its Mods for another... assuming you've got a loose Legendary Mod, and some Scrip, that is.    To craft Legendary Mods, head to the Tinker's workbench. You'll need to know the Recipe for the Mod, and have a stack of Legendary Modules to boot.    Scrip and Legendary Mod Recipes can both be found by scrapping Legendary Weapons, Armor and Power Armor at any workbench. You'll always receive Scrip, and in rare cases, you'll learn the Recipe of one of the Legendary Mods attached to the item you scrapped. If you're lucky, you may even get a loose Mod that can be attached right away!    Each time a Legendary Mod is replaced on a Legendary Item, the cost in Scrip will gradually increase.    Legendary Modules can be obtained from a vendor named The Purveyor at the Rusty Pick for Scrip or as rewards for certain content such as Expeditions. Scrip is obtained by trading Legendary Items at the Legendary Exchange vending machine or scrapping Legendary Weapons, Armor and Power Armor at any workbench. Legendary Exchange vending machines can be found at the Rusty Pick or any train station.    Once a Legendary Mod has been replaced on a Legendary Armor, Power Armor, or on a Weapon, that Legendary Item can no longer be traded with other players or dropped without destroying it. However, they can still be placed into your STASH.

items.name: Legendary Perks
items.desc: Legendary Perks are special abilities that can greatly enhance almost any aspect of your character or teammates.     Unlocking and Equipping Legendary Perks  Your first Legendary Perk Slot opens at level 50 and you periodically gain new slots as you level up.    You can equip Legendary Perks through the Legendary Perk Menu, which can be opened with the button at the top of the Perk Menu.    Legendary Perk Ranks  Legendary Perks can be upgraded with Perk Coins. You can earn Perk Coins by scrapping regular Perk Cards.

items.name: Level 50 Character Boost
items.desc: The Level 50 Character Boost increases your active character's level to 50. The Level 50 Character Boost is not available to characters if they are already level 50 or above.    In addition to increasing the character's level, the Level 50 Boost grants the character a Perk Loadout and equipment that are level-appropriate. The Perk Loadout and equipment are automatically equipped to the character. Any Perks or equipment that were previously equipped will still be in the character's Perk Menu or Inventory.    If the character that was boosted is deleted, the Loadout and levels will be lost.

items.name: Leveling Up
items.desc: Leveling up allows you to increase one of your SPECIAL stats, gives you choice of a new Perk, and helps you meet the level requirements for certain equipment.    As you complete quests, defeat enemies, and explore the world, you'll earn Experience Points (XP). Once you've gained sufficient XP, your level will increase.     Open your Pip-Boy and press [YButton]. This will open the Level Up menu. You'll be asked to choose one of your SPECIAL stats to increase. You'll also get to choose a new Perk.    (Note: You will stop receiving SPECIAL increases once your level is higher than 50, but you'll still be able to choose a new Perk.)    After you've made your selections, you'll enter the Perk menu. You can re-assign all your Perks from here. The bottom row of cards are your available Perks, the top row of cards are all the Perks you have equipped.    When you equip a Perk, it is assigned to its associated SPECIAL stat. The Gladiator Perk is a Strength Perk, for example, and goes into your Strength slot when it is equipped.    There is a limit to the number of Perks that each SPECIAL stat can hold. Every Perk has a number in the upper-left corner. This is how many points the Perk is worth. Your total number of Perk points can't exceed the associated SPECIAL stat. For example, if your Strength is 3, then you cannot have more than 3 points worth of Strength Perks. Whether you choose to equip several low point Perks or one high point Perk, is up to you.    You can exit the Perk menu at any time by pressing [Cancel].    You can choose to reallocate your SPECIAL stats by visiting a Punch Card Machine beginning at level 25.    Level Requirements for Items  Some Weapons, Armor, and Power Armor pieces have a minimum level requirement to use them. You won't be able to equip an item if you aren't the appropriate level or higher.    You can see the minimum level of an item by going to the Items category in the Pip-Boy and selecting the item.

items.name: Locking Items
items.desc: Lock your valued items in your Pip-Boy and C.A.M.P. Menus.    Locked items are protected from being  - Dropped  - Sold  - Scrapped  - Transferred (see Game Settings)  - Consumed (see Game Settings)    Please note: Locked items are not prevented from being used in crafting.

items.name: Lunchboxes
items.desc: Lunchboxes are consumable items that you can open to gain a boost to the Experience Points (XP) you earn as well as one of eight random Buff Effects. Additionally, any player in your vicinity when opening a Lunchbox will also receive the XP Boost as well as one of the possible buff effects. Other players may not get the same effect as you.     XP Boost  Each Lunchbox that affects you increases the XP you gain from all sources by 25%. This effect will stack up to 100% total bonus. Any Lunchboxes that affect you when you are at the 100% bonus effect will refresh the effect timer.   The XP Boost lasts for 60 minutes and is paused when you leave the game.     Buff Effects  Each Lunchbox applies a buff effect to an affected player in addition to the XP Boost. There are 8 possible effects, and players can only have a single copy of an effect on them at a time; if the player were to receive the same effect, the timer for the effect is refreshed. The Buff effect lasts for 60 minutes and is paused when you leave the game.   Available Buff Effects are:  - Gift Bag - Increased Carry Weight.  - Confetti Mess - Adds colorful explosions to some creature deaths.  - Plastic Animals - Increased damage to Animals.  - So Much Cake - Reduce Hunger gain.  - Fingertrap - Increased damage to Super Mutant enemies.  - Antacids - Increased Radiation resistance.  - Noisemaker - Increased damage to Robot enemies.   - To-go Punch - Reduce Thirst gain.    Effect Odds  Players have a 100% chance to receive the XP Boost effect from a Lunchbox.  Players have a 100% chance to receive a Buff Effect; there is a 12.5% chance to receive a particular Buff Effect from a Lunchbox.    Notes  While we currently have no plans to change the odds, we reserve the right to update or modify information shown above at our discretion to reflect changes and/or evolving reporting standards.  Lunchboxes are not available for purchase in some territories.    Last Updated: 10/07/2020

items.name: Map
items.desc: The Map allows you to navigate Appalachia, fast travel to locations, and set your own custom markers.    Open the Map at any time by pressing [Map].    To adjust your view, use [LeftStick] to move the cursor across the map. Use [RightStick] to zoom in and out.      Map Icons  - Building icons are locations you have visited. You can activate a location to fast travel to it.    - Custom icons can be set for the locations of you and your Teammates' C.A.M.P.s. You can activate the C.A.M.P. to fast travel to it.    - Diamond icons are quest targets for your active quests. You can activate a quest target to stop tracking it.    - Black square with a gold outline icons are quest targets for a quest that both you and your Team Leader have active.    - Circled areas are area quest targets for your active quests.    - Hexagon icons are Activities that are currently active in Appalachia. You can activate an Activity to join the Activity and fast travel to it.    - Hexagon with three player icons are Public Events that are currently active in Appalachia. You can activate and join Public Events in the same manner as Activities.    - Yellow dots represent other Players. Red dots represent hostile Players.    - A yellow dot with a star inside is your Team Leader. You can activate your Team Leader or any other Teammate to fast travel to them.      Custom Markers  You can also place custom markers on the map, which will then appear on your compass as you travel the world.     To place a custom marker, move your cursor to the desired spot on the map and press [Accept]. To remove a custom marker, move the cursor to an empty spot and press [Accept], then select "Remove Marker.

items.name: Mutations
items.desc: Mutations give you a mixture of powerful positive and negative effects. Whenever you take Radiation damage, you have a chance to gain a Mutation. You cannot gain Mutations if you are below Level 5.    You can see the effects of any Mutations you have by opening the Pip-Boy and going to Stat -> Effects.    Mutations are semi-permanent. Every time you use RadAway, there is a chance that a Mutation will be removed. You can keep using RadAway for more attempts to remove a Mutation.    Serums are consumable items that will grant a specific Mutation as soon as you use it. If you already have that Mutation, the Serum will temporarily suppress the negative effects of the Mutation.

items.name: Onslaught
items.desc: Onslaught is a stacking buff found on Perks and items. By default, direct attacks against targets generate Onslaught stacks and refreshes their duration. You lose one stack every second. The benefits you gain from each stack varies by the Perks and items you have equipped. Some Perks can change how you gain and lose Onslaught stacks.

items.name: Pacifist Mode
items.desc: Pacifist Mode is an option to completely opt-out of all PvP activity. You will deal no damage to other Players, and other Players will not deal damage to you. Messages intended for PvP activity are also turned off.    To turn on Pacifist Mode, press [Map] to open your Map, then [LShoulder] to open the Main Menu. Select "Settings -> Game" and then select Pacifist Mode. You can turn Pacifist Mode off or on at any time once you hit level 5.

items.name: Perk Card Packs
items.desc: Perk Card Packs are consumable items that can be opened to receive 4 random Perk Cards and a random pack of bubblegum. Perk Cards received are independent of currently owned or equipped Perk Cards. It is possible to receive Perk Cards from Perk Card Packs that have level requirements that exceed the player's current level.  For more information about Perks, see the Help section on Perks.    Unwanted or excess Perk Cards can be scrapped into Perk Coins, which are used to upgrade Legendary Perks. For more information about Legendary Perks, see the Help section on Legendary Perks.    When Perk Card Packs are received, they can be opened in the Level Up menu. To access the Level Up menu, open your Pip-Boy and press [YButton].

items.name: Perks
items.desc: Perks are special abilities that can affect everything from the damage you deal in combat, to your ability to help your teammates, to being able to open locks and hack terminals.       Leveling Up and Choosing Perks  Each time you gain a level, you'll be granted a SPECIAL increase and a Perk. Once your level is higher than 50, this changes. Instead, when you level up, you will have the option to pick a new Perk.    Open your Pip-Boy and press [YButton]. This will open the Level Up menu. You'll be asked to choose one of your SPECIAL stats to increase. You'll also get to choose a new Perk.      Perk Menu  After you've made your selections, you'll enter the Perk menu. You can re-assign all your Perks from here. The bottom row of cards are your available Perks, the top row of cards are all the Perks you have equipped.    When you equip a Perk, it is assigned to its associated SPECIAL stat. The Gladiator Perk is a Strength Perk, for example, and goes into your Strength slot when it is equipped.    There is a limit to the number of Perks that each SPECIAL stat can hold. Every Perk has a number in the upper-left corner. This is how many points the Perk is worth. Your total number of Perk points can't exceed the associated SPECIAL stat. For example, if your Strength is 3, then you cannot have more than 3 points worth of Strength Perks. Whether you choose to equip several low point Perks or one high point Perk, is up to you.    You can exit the Perk menu at any time by pressing [Cancel]. You can return to the Perk menu by opening the Pip-Boy and pressing [YButton].      Perk Ranks  Some Perks have multiple ranks. You can rank up a Perk by combining it with a duplicate. For example, two Gladiator rank one Perks can be combined to produce one Gladiator rank two Perk.    To rank up a Perk, first equip the Perk, then press [XButton]. This will consume the duplicate Perk.      Sharing Perks  You can select a Perk that will be shared to all members of your Team. Enter the Perk Menu, select an equipped Perk, then press [YButton].     Your Charisma limits which perks you can share. To share a Perk worth 1 point, you must have a Charisma of 3 or more. To share a Perk worth 2 points, you must have a Charisma of 6 or more. Perks worth 3 points require a Charisma of 9. Perks worth 4 points require a Charisma of 12. And finally, Perks worth 5 points require a Charisma of 15.    Perks you select to Share will be applied only to members of your Team. If you leave the Team, or the Team is disbanded, you will automatically stop sharing the Perk with those Players.    Race-Exclusive Perks  A selection of perks will be exclusive to the Human or Ghoul race. Any Perk that is not compatible with the current race will be locked and not allowed to equip. You can scrap incompatible perks for Perk Coins.

items.name: Perks
items.desc: Perks are special abilities that can affect everything from the damage you deal in combat, to your ability to help your teammates, to being able to open locks and hack terminals.       Leveling Up and Choosing Perks  Each time you gain a level, you'll be granted a SPECIAL increase and a Perk. Once your level is higher than 50, this changes. Instead, when you level up, you will have the option to pick a new Perk.    Open your Pip-Boy and press [YButton]. This will open the Level Up menu. You'll be asked to choose one of your SPECIAL stats to increase. You'll also get to choose a new Perk.      Perk Menu  After you've made your selections, you'll enter the Perk menu. You can re-assign all your Perks from here. The bottom row of cards are your available Perks, the top row of cards are all the Perks you have equipped.    When you equip a Perk, it is assigned to its associated SPECIAL stat. The Gladiator Perk is a Strength Perk, for example, and goes into your Strength slot when it is equipped.    There is a limit to the number of Perks that each SPECIAL stat can hold. Every Perk has a number in the upper-left corner. This is how many points the Perk is worth. Your total number of Perk points can't exceed the associated SPECIAL stat. For example, if your Strength is 3, then you cannot have more than 3 points worth of Strength Perks. Whether you choose to equip several low point Perks or one high point Perk, is up to you.    You can exit the Perk menu at any time by pressing [Cancel]. You can return to the Perk menu by opening the Pip-Boy and pressing [YButton].      Perk Ranks  Some Perks have multiple ranks. You can rank up a Perk by combining it with a duplicate. For example, two Gladiator rank one Perks can be combined to produce one Gladiator rank two Perk.    To rank up a Perk, first equip the Perk, then press [XButton]. This will consume the duplicate Perk.      Sharing Perks  You can select a Perk that will be shared to all members of your Team. Enter the Perk Menu, select an equipped Perk, then press [YButton].     Your Charisma limits which perks you can share. To share a Perk worth 1 point, you must have a Charisma of 3 or more. To share a Perk worth 2 points, you must have a Charisma of 6 or more. Perks worth 3 points require a Charisma of 9. Perks worth 4 points require a Charisma of 12. And finally, Perks worth 5 points require a Charisma of 15.    Perks you select to Share will be applied only to members of your Team. If you leave the Team, or the Team is disbanded, you will automatically stop sharing the Perk with those Players.    Race-Exclusive Perks  A selection of perks will be exclusive to the Human or Ghoul race. Any Perk that is not compatible with the current race will be locked and not allowed to equip. You can scrap incompatible perks for Perk Coins.

items.name: Picking Locks
items.desc: Picking locks will let you open doors and containers.    Locks have a difficulty level, usually between 0 and 3. A level 0 lock can always be picked, but higher-level locks will require you to equip Perks.    There are 3 Pick Lock Perks: Picklock, Expert Picklock, and Master Picklock. Each Perk you equip increases your Picklock Skill by 1. You will need to equip all 3 Perks to pick level 3 locks.    To pick a lock, you must have at least one bobby pin in your inventory. Bobby pins can be found as you explore Appalachia, purchased from robot vendors, or traded for with other Players. Once you have a bobby pin, approach the locked door or container you want to pick and press [Activate].     To pick the lock, use [RotatePick] to rotate the bobby pin, then [RotateLock] to rotate the screwdriver.     If the lock resists, release [RotateLock] and reposition the bobby pin before trying again. The closer the bobby pin is to the correct position, the further the lock will rotate before you either encounter resistance or the bobby pin breaks.     When the bobby pin is in the correct position, the lock will fully rotate and open. More difficult locks require more precise placement of the bobby pin.    Press [Cancel] to exit lockpicking.    Some locks require a key or cannot be opened through lockpicking.

items.name: Ping System
items.desc: The Ping System is a player communication tool that allows players to place visual highlights in the world.    Players can use the ping system to highlight actors, objects, interactions and paths for all teammates to see and is greatly beneficial for relaying information in the heat of a battle and for teams without group chats enabled.     Players can place pings into game world by holding [QuickkeyDown]. This can be swapped with Emotes in Gameplay Options.    The placed ping is contextual and will change form and color based on the type of object highlighted    Placing a ping in the world will contextually indicate one of the following to all team members:           Yellow Ping Icon -- Default / No Contextual Target         Orange Ping Icon -- Containers        Blue Ping Icon -- Activators        Red Ping Icon -- Enemy Actor        Green Ping Icon -- Friendly Actor        Grey Ping Icon -- Dead Actor     Pings are only visible to teammates in proximity to the player who placed the ping, or who are in the same interior location.    Pings that are off-screen will stick to the edge of the screen in the direction of the ping.

items.name: Power
items.desc: Many building objects require Power to function. To provide Power to an object, you'll need to hook it up to an existing generator or build a new one from the Building menu in the Generators tab.    Power is shared between most objects by wires. You can run a wire between two objects by switching to the Modify mode by pressing [Pipboy]. Highlight one of the objects and press [YButton] to run the wire.     Objects that are within range of the wire will be highlighted in white. Highlight one of them and press [YButton] again and the two objects will now be connected by a wire.    All objects that are connected together by wires are considered a "power grid," and can use all Power produced within the connected grid. This means you can hook up multiple generators into a power grid in order to provide Power to everything on the grid.    The direction of the wires doesn't matter; Power can flow freely around the grid as long as there is some wired connection between the generator and the object that needs Power.    Highlighting a generator will also highlight all objects that are part of its power grid. Highlighting an object that requires Power will also show if it is currently powered; if the "Requires Power" icon is red, then the object isn't currently receiving Power.     This means that either the object isn't hooked up to a power source at all, or that the power grid that it is attached to is overloaded; there isn't enough power on the grid to supply all the objects that need it.    Wires have a limited range; if you need to run wires a long distance, build objects from the Power Connectors tab to bridge the gap. These include switched versions, which allow you to turn power on and off to anything connected to the switch.    Some objects, such as lightbulbs, receive Power simply from being near a power connector, like a Power Pylon, rather than using a direct wired connection.

items.name: Power Armor
items.desc: Power Armor is the most advanced form of protection you can find. It provides the following benefits:    - Significantly reduces incoming damage.    - Increases melee damage.    - Increases carry weight.    - Prevents all damage from falling.    - With a helmet equipped, increases how long you can stay underwater.    Walk up to a suit of Power Armor and press [Activate] to enter it.    To exit a suit of Power Armor, hold [Activate].      Claiming Power Armor  You can claim any suit of Power Armor that another Player does not own. To claim the Power Armor, enter it by walking up to the suit and pressing [Activate].    If you are told that you are not high enough level to enter the Power Armor, then you can still claim the Power Armor Frame by stripping the armor pieces from the suit. Press [QCOpenTransferMenu] to open the Transfer menu and remove all the armor pieces. Then try to enter the suit again.      Collecting and Recalling  Once you claim a suit of Power Armor, you can place it in your inventory by exiting the suit and then pressing [YButton:20] to collect the Power Armor. Your suit will be added to your inventory under Item -> Armor with the name Power Armor Chassis.    Your Power Armor will also automatically be recalled to your inventory if you exit it and leave the area, disconnect, or after a period of time has passed.      Deploying and Dropping  You can deploy your Power Armor from your inventory by opening your Pip-Boy, selecting Power Armor Chassis, then pressing [Activate]. You will need to place the Power Armor in a valid spot, which will turn the highlight around the armor blue.    Deployed Power Armor is owned by you, and other Players cannot enter it. As the owner, the Power Armor will be recalled into your inventory if you do not enter it.    If you want to give up ownership of the Power Armor, you can select it from your inventory and press [XButton] to drop it. Dropped Power Armor will appear next to you in the world and can be claimed by any other Player.       Fusion Cores  Power Armor runs on Fusion Cores. Performing any of the following actions will reduce your Power Armor core's charge:     - Running    - Sprinting    - Power Attacks    - V.A.T.S.     Once your Fusion Core has been emptied, you will move at a reduced rate and will be unable to Power Attack or use V.A.T.S.    If you have another Fusion Core in your inventory when your current core runs out, it will automatically be installed in your suit. Otherwise, you'll either need to find a new core to restore your Power Armor's functionality.       Power Armor Pieces  All Power Armor is made of two major components: a frame and a set of armor pieces.     Each armor piece attached to your frame increases your Damage Resistance, but a Power Armor frame does not require armor pieces to function. A frame without armor pieces will still provide protection against falling, increased melee damage, extra carry weight, and some Damage Resistance.    Armor pieces can become damaged over time. While in your Power Armor, the current state of your armor pieces is visible on the suit icon to the left of the screen. Pieces in red have taken significant damage and should be repaired. Empty sections mean a piece is either missing or destroyed and must be replaced.    You can view an armor piece's current Condition by opening your Pip-Boy and going to Item -> Armor, or by using a Power Armor Station.    To add or remove an armor piece from your frame, open your Pip-Boy and go to Item -> Armor, select the piece you want to add or remove, then press [Activate].    You can also equip or unequip armor pieces at a Power Armor station or by approaching your Power Armor suit and pressing [QCOpenTransferMenu] to open the Transfer menu.      Power Armor Stations  A Power Armor Station allows you to craft new armor pieces, modify existing pieces, and make repairs to pieces.     In order to use a Power Armor Station, first walk into the station while wearing the Power Armor, then exit out of the armor. Then walk over to the Power Armor Station and press [Activate].

items.name: Private Teams
items.desc: Private Teams are groups of Players composed of one Team Leader and 1-3 Teammates.    You can invite another Player to join your Team by walking up to them and pressing [Activate]. You can also invite Players on your Friends list by using the Social Menu, or by selecting them on the Map.    The Player you invite will need to open the Social Menu and select you in order to accept your request.      Social Menu  The Social Menu is where you can manage your Friends and your Team.    You can open the Social Menu by holding [Map]. You can also get to the Social Menu by opening the Map by pressing [Map] and then pressing [RShoulder].    Use [Move] to navigate the Social Menu. Left and right on the stick will navigate between the Friends, Team, and Recent Players lists. Up and down on the stick will allow you to select a Player. Press [Accept] to open the options list for that Player, which includes things like inviting them to join your team or adding them to your Friends list.      Team Leader  The Player that initially invites other Players to join their Private Team becomes the Team Leader. The Team Leader can kick Players off the Team or promote another Player to be Team Leader instead.    Open the Social Menu and go to the Team category, then select a Player on your team and press [Accept] to open the list of options. You can then select "Kick" and "Promote to Leader" from here.      Perk Sharing  You can select a Perk that will be shared to all members of your Team. Enter the Perk Menu, select an equipped Perk, then press [YButton]. You can only share Perks that have a point value equal to or lower than your Charisma.      Fast Travel  You can fast travel to your Team Leader or Teammates for free by selecting them on the Map.      Leave Team  You can leave a team by opening the Social Menu, select your profile and then select "Leave Team.

items.name: PvP
items.desc: PvP (Player versus Player) combat is when two or more Players attack each other. PvP has the following rules:    - Players must be at least Level 5 to engage in PvP.    - When attacking another Player no damage is dealt until both Players have hit each other.    - Once both Players have hit each other they become Hostile to each other. Hostile Players show up as red dots on the compass.    - Teams follow the same PvP rules for determining if a Player is Hostile. Each member of a Team will be determined Hostile individually.      Pacifist Mode    Pacifist Mode is on by default and prevents you from dealing damage to other Players and other Players will always deal reduced damage to you. Messages intended for PvP activity are also turned off.    To turn off Pacifist Mode, press [Map] to open your Map, then [LShoulder] to open the Main Menu. Select "Settings -> Game" and then select Pacifist Mode. You can turn Pacifist Mode off or on at any time.

Selecting a quest in the Main, Side, or Daily sections and pressing [RShoulder] will display the location of the selected quest's current objective on your map.

items.name: Radiation
items.desc: Exposure to radiation causes radiation damage (or "rads"), reducing your maximum health.    The amount of rads you've accumulated is displayed in red on your HP bar. Your Pip-Boy also has a built-in radiation indicator on the right of its screen.    You can gain rads by consuming tainted foods and beverages or being exposed to an irradiated environment. If your Pip-Boy's Geiger counter starts to click, it means you've entered an irradiated area.     The amount of rads you are currently gaining will be displayed above your HP bar. If you're in Power Armor, your current rad intake will be displayed on the "Rads" dial next to your Hit Points.    You can slow the accumulation of rads by increasing your Radiation Resistance. You can find your current Radiation Resistance in the Pip-Boy under Stat -> Status. Rad-X, clothing, armor, and certain perks can also up your Radiation Resistance.     Use RadAway to cure radiation damage.
