items.desc: Any radio station broadcasting in your current area will be displayed on the Radio tab in the Pip-Boy. To listen in, select a station with [Click].    While a station is active, you can enter or exit the Pip-Boy and your selected station will continue to play.

items.name: Re-Roller
items.desc: Re-Rollers are a consumable item that you can use to re-roll a Daily or Weekly challenge.    Re-rolling Challenges  Daily or Weekly Challenges can be re-rolled from the Challenges screen.  - Players are given one free re-roll per day. This free re-roll can be used on a Daily or Weekly Challenge. FO1st members are granted one extra free re-roll per day.  - When a player has used up all of their free re-rolls they are able to use a Re-Roller to make additional re-rolls. Each Re-Roller consumed grants one additional re-roll.  - If a challenge is re-rolled any progress already made towards completing that challenge is lost.  Not all challenges can be re-rolled:  - Completed challenges cannot be re-rolled.  - Challenges the player does not have access to cannot be re-rolled (for example, if a player is not a FO1st member they will be unable to re-roll FO1st challenges).    Effect Odds  - When a challenge is re-rolled a new challenge will be selected at random.  - When re-rolling a challenge players have a 25% chance of the new challenge being an Epic Challenge. Epic Challenges are more difficult to complete and are worth more S.C.O.R.E. XP than a regular challenge.    Notes  While we currently have no plans to change the odds, we reserve the right to update or modify information shown above at our discretion to reflect changes and/or evolving reporting standards.  Re-Rollers are not available for purchase in some territories.

items.name: S.C.O.R.E. Booster Item
items.desc: The S.C.O.R.E. Booster is a consumable item that temporarily grants 25% bonus S.C.O.R.E. whenever you would gain S.C.O.R.E. from completing challenges.    Using the S.C.O.R.E. Booster Item  - A S.C.O.R.E. Booster item can be activated from the Challenges menu or Scoreboard screen.  - Once consumed, you will gain 25% bonus S.C.O.R.E. any time you earn S.C.O.R.E. from completing challenges. The effect lasts for 24 hours, starting from the moment the item was consumed.  - While active the S.C.O.R.E. Booster item affects all characters on your account.  - Only one S.C.O.R.E. Booster item can be active at a time.   - The effect from the S.C.O.R.E. Booster item stacks with the S.C.O.R.E. Boost rewards on the Season Scoreboard.

items.name: Scout's Banners
items.desc: Scout's Banners are consumable items that you can open to gain various buffs that help you in combat: Scout's Call, Scout's Code, and Scout's Courage. Scout's Call is a buff that adds a 5% (max 20%) chance to trigger a Scout's Code buff when you kill an enemy. Scout's Codes are various buffs that are designed to help you keep fighting. Each Scout's Banner applies a random Scout's Code. Scout's Courage is a buff that will automatically revive you with a Stimpak if you are incapacitated, once every 5 minutes.     Opening a Scout's Banner will apply Scout's Call, a random Scout's Code, and Scout's Courage not just to you but any player in your vicinity. Other players may not get the same Scout's Code as you.     Scout's Call:  Scout's Call gives a 5 - 20% chance to trigger ALL active Scout's Code buffs when you kill an enemy. Each Scout's Banner that affects you increases the odds of triggering Scout's Code buffs by 5%. This effect will stack up to 20% total trigger chance. Any Scout's Banners that affect you when you are at the 20% bonus effect will refresh the effect timer. Scout's Call lasts for 60 minutes and is paused when you leave the game.     Scout's Code:  Each Scout's Banner applies a random Scout's Code to the player. Scout's Codes are effects that get triggered if Scout's Call is triggered on an enemy. There are 5 possible effects, and players can only have a single copy of an effect on them at a time; if the player were to receive the same effect, the timer for the effect is refreshed. The Buff effect lasts for 60 minutes and is paused when you leave the game.     Available Buff Effects are:  - Teamwork - Restore 100% AP.   - Survival - Restore 20% HP.   - Innovation - Repair 10% Weapon CND.  - Discovery - Highlight enemies for 5s.   - Research - Repair 10% Armor CND.    Scout's Courage:   Scout's Courage gives the player 100% chance to auto-revive when incapacitated. This effect is on a 5 minute cooldown. Any Scout's Banners that affect you when you already have Scout's Courage applied will recast the effect.The Buff effect lasts for 60 minutes and is paused when you leave the game.     Effect Odds:  Players have a 100% chance to receive the Scout's Call effect from a Scout Banner.  Players have a 100% chance to receive a Scout's Code effect from a Scout Banner; there is a 20% chance to receive a particular Scout's Code from a Scout Banner.  Players have a 100% chance to receive the Scout's Courage effect from a Scout Banner.    Notes:  While we currently have no plans to change the odds, we reserve the right to update or modify information shown above at our discretion to reflect changes and/or evolving reporting standards.  Scout's Banners are not available for purchase in some territories.    Last Updated: 09/01/2022

items.name: Seasons
items.desc: Each new Season offers a collection of themed rewards that are available to be claimed only for the duration of the Season. Complete in-game activities to earn S.C.O.R.E. and Rank Up. Each Rank earned grants you Tickets that you can redeem to claim Season Rewards.      Complete Challenges to earn S.C.O.R.E.  Earn S.C.O.R.E. by completing Challenges. Challenges are given daily and weekly and require completing a variety of in-game activities such as killing certain types of creatures or finding and collecting items in the world.      Ranking Up  When you accumulate enough S.C.O.R.E. you will Rank Up. Each new Rank you earn grants you 25 Tickets.    It is also possible to purchase Ranks for 150 Atoms per Rank up to Rank 150.    You can continue to earn S.C.O.R.E. and Rank Up beyond Rank 100.      Redeem Tickets to claim Season Rewards   The Tickets you earn from ranking up can be redeemed for rewards on the Seasons screen.    Access the Seasons screen from the Main Menu or from within game by pressing [Map] to open your Map, then [LShoulder] to open the Main Menu and selecting "Seasons".    Seasons Rewards are listed across multiple pages with each page containing several rewards. Access to the first page of rewards is automatic. A Access additional pages by Ranking Up to the required Season Rank.    You can claim any available rewards by redeeming the required number of Tickets. The Tickets required for each Season Reward vary, with smaller rewards typically requiring fewer Tickets than larger rewards. Occasionally rewards may require 0 Tickets and are free to claim as soon as the page is unlocked.      Fallout First Season Rewards  The Fallout First Season Rewards for a particular Season are only available to players with an active Fallout 1st subscription during the relevant Season or players that have purchased the specific Fallout First Season Pass. To claim these rewards you must also have access to the page they are on and have enough Tickets to redeem the reward.      End of Season  A Season Pass will apply to a specific Season and will expire at the end of that Season. Rewards and Season Rank are unique to the specific Season and therefore, when a Season ends, any unclaimed Rewards will no longer be available and a player's Season Rank progress and Ticket balance accumulated in one Season will not carry onto the next Season.

items.name: Shelters
items.desc: Shelters are instanced interiors that act as expansions to your C.A.M.P. Each Shelter has its own workshop budget, which is roughly 1.5x your normal C.A.M.P. budget.     Entrances  Shelters are accessed by placing Shelter Entrances in your C.A.M.P.. Once a Shelter entrance is placed it can be used to teleport you into one of your Shelters.You can even place entrances inside Shelters to create a "daisy chain" effect!  You can place multiple Shelter entrances of any type, but all entrances of a certain type will lead to the same instance of their associated Shelter. For example, you can place three Vault Atrium Shelter entrances separately, but all three will lead you to the same instance of your Vault Atrium Shelter.   Shelter entrances can be locked and unlocked like regular workshop doors. Locked Shelter entrances can be lock picked like other workshop doors.     Building  Building in Shelters may feel different than building in Appalachia does. Some workshop rules have been relaxed or removed. Items will not require support and are allowed to float. The floors in your Shelter also act as foundations, so you can build structures directly on top of them. You can toggle workshop snapping rules on and off in the workshop menu using [ReadyWeapon].   Each Shelter comes with a built in Shelters Control Panel, which you can use to enter workshop mode, Scrap All in your current Shelter, or Repair All in your current Shelter.   Some workshop categories have been blacklisted in Shelters. You cannot build Allies, Food, Water, Resources.    Social  Shelters support PVP encounters. If you are hostile to another player on the surface you will retain your PVP status when you enter a Shelter. The inverse is also true - if you become hostile to another player inside a Shelter your hostile status will be retained if you return to the surface. If you die inside a Shelter you will not drop a loot bag.   Shelters also support building in teams. You can build in your teammates' Shelters and they can build in yours.    Paper Map  If you or one of your teammates places a Shelter at your C.A.M.P. and leaves it unlocked, you will see a small "Shelters" icon next to that C.A.M.P. on the paper map.

items.name: Sleeping
items.desc: You can sleep in a bed, cot, mat, or sleeping bag.    Sleeping will slowly heal you over time. Depending on certain conditions, and if you sleep long enough, you will receive one of the following effects:    Rested - 5% XP gain for 60mins (Sleeping Bag)  Well Rested - 5% XP gain for 120mins (Bed)  Kindred Spirit - 5% XP gain for 180mins (Bed with ally present in C.A.M.P.)  Lover's Embrace - 5% XP gain for 180mins (Bed with romanced ally present in C.A.M.P.)    Sleeping on mattresses or sleeping bags on the ground has a chance to give you a Disease.

items.name: Small Guns
items.desc: Small Guns refers to weapons tagged as Pistol, Rifle, or Shotgun and excludes weapons tagged as Heavy Gun and Bow.

items.name: Sneaking
items.desc: Press [Sneak] to sneak. Sneaking allows you to avoid detection by enemies.     While sneaking, your current level of detection will be displayed on screen. There are four levels of detection:     Hidden  No nearby characters detect you. While hidden, any attacks you make are considered "Sneak Attacks" and deal increased damage, but attacking risks exposing your position.     The brackets around the word "HIDDEN" indicate how close you are to being detected. The further apart the brackets, the more successful your sneaking.    Detected  Non-hostile characters nearby have been alerted to your presence.     Caution  Enemies have detected you and are actively searching for you. If you can evade them for long enough, they will return to their previous activity.     The further apart the brackets around "CAUTION," the closer you are to returning to "HIDDEN."     Attacks made while in Caution still count as Sneak Attacks.     Danger  Enemies have spotted you and will begin attacking.     Successful sneaking is affected by a number of factors:    Light Level  The darker the spot you're sneaking in, the harder it will be for enemies to spot you. If you're close to being detected, try ducking into the shadows to remain hidden.    Line of Sight  If enemies don't have line of sight to you, they're much less likely to detect you.    Movement  You're hardest to detect while motionless and easier to spot while moving. It's significantly harder to sneak while moving quickly (although this can be improved with perks).    Sound  Attacking with unsilenced or heavy weapons makes noise, which may alert enemies to your presence.    Armor  The higher the weight of your armor, the more noise it makes while moving. Sneaking is extremely challenging in Power Armor.     Enemies will also react to loud noises in the environment. If you can trigger an explosion or trap without being detected, you can lure away unsuspecting enemies.

items.name: Social
items.desc: The Social Menu is where you can manage your Friends and your Team.    You can open the Social Menu by holding [Map]. You can also get to the Social Menu by opening the Map by pressing [Map] and then pressing [RShoulder].    Use [Move] to navigate the Social Menu. Left and right on the stick will navigate between the Friends, Team, and Recent Players lists. Up and down on the stick will allow you to select a Player. Press [Accept] to open the options list for that Player, which includes things like inviting them to join your team or adding them to your Friends list.    The Social Menu also contains a Public Teams tab. Use [Move] to navigate the list of Public Teams and press [Activate] to join one.    You can create a Public Team by selecting the "Create New Team" option in the Public Teams tab. Selecting this option opens a menu to choose a goal for your new Public Team. Use [Move] to navigate the list of goals and press [Activate] to create a new team with the selected goal. There are various goals that each offer a unique bonus to all members of the Public Team. Creating a new Public Team will send a notification to every Player currently in the world, inviting them to join your team.

items.desc: The Social Menu is where you can manage your Friends and your Team.    You can open the Social Menu by opening the Map by pressing [Map] and then pressing [RShoulder].    Use the mouse to navigate the Social Menu. [Click] on the Friends, Team, and Recent tabs to open that list of Players. Then click on a Player to open the options list for that Player, which includes things like inviting them to join your team or adding them to your Friends list.    The Social Menu also contains a Public Teams tab. Use the mouse to navigate the list of Public Teams and [Click] on a Public Team to join it. This will add you to the Public Team if it is not full.    You can create a Public Team by selecting the "Create New Team" option in the Public Teams tab. Selecting this option opens a menu to choose a goal for your new Public Team. Use the mouse to navigate the list of goals and [Click] on a goal to create a new team with the selected goal. There are various goals that each offer a unique bonus to all members of the Public Team. Creating a new Public Team will send a notification to every Player currently in the world, inviting them to join your team.

items.name: SPECIAL
items.desc: The SPECIAL attributes define your natural abilities, affecting everything from how much damage you deal to how well you can craft items.    Strength  Strength is a measure of your raw physical power. It affects how much you can carry, and the damage of all melee attacks.    Perception  Perception affects your awareness of nearby enemies, your ability to detect stealthy movement, and your weapon accuracy in V.A.T.S.    Endurance  Endurance is a measure of your overall physical fitness. It affects your total Health, the Action Point drain from sprinting, and your resistance to disease.    Charisma  Charisma is your ability to lead and help others. It allows you to share higher point Perks and also affects your rewards from Group Quests and prices when you barter.    Intelligence  Intelligence is a measure of overall mental acuity, affects ability to hack terminals, condition and durability of crafted items, experience gained, and returns from scrapping.    Agility  Agility is a measure of your overall finesse and reflexes. It affects the number of Action Points in V.A.T.S. and your ability to sneak.    Luck  Luck is a measure of your general good fortune, and affects the recharge rate of Critical Hits as well as the condition and durability of items that you loot.      Improving SPECIAL Attributes  You can permanently improve any of your SPECIAL attributes when you Level Up.     SPECIAL attributes can also be temporarily improved by wearing certain gear or consuming food and chems.    SPECIAL attributes have a maximum value of 15 and can never be raised beyond that, even from temporary buffs.      Perks Requirements  Most perks have a SPECIAL requirement. You'll be unable to take such perks until you've raised the required SPECIAL attribute to the necessary amount.    Note that temporary SPECIAL bonuses (like those from chems, clothes, etc.) don't count towards perk requirements.

items.name: SPECIAL Loadouts
items.desc: S.P.E.C.I.A.L. Loadouts is a new feature that's automatically unlocked at level 25 that allows you to customize and name sets of perk cards and S.P.E.C.I.A.L. configurations and quickly change between them by using the new Punch Card Machine.      Punchcard Machine  The Punchcard Machine is a C.A.M.P. item. The recipe for this is learned automatically upon reaching Level 25 and can be crafted in the workshop Build Menu. Place the Punchcard Machine on a flat surface within your C.A.M.P. and interact with it to view the Loadouts Menu. Punchcard Machines can also be found at train stations across the world.      Loadout Slots  You can purchase additional Slots from the Atomic Shop and purchasing an additional slot is account wide, so any additional slots that you purchase will be available to all characters on your account.      Unallocated Points  Players with a loudout that has unallocated S.P.E.C.I.A.L. will automatically go to the Edit SPECIAL screen when first switching to the loadout. They are free to cancel this operation and continue with unallocated points if they choose.      Switching Loadouts  SPECIAL Point allocations are easily switched within the Punchcard Machine menu by highlighting the Loadout Slot you wish to load in and selecting it.      Ranking Up Cards  Ranking up a card that is in use by multiple loadouts will display a message if any of those loadouts can no longer support the card's new rank value. In some cases, you may want to have the same cards with different ranks to assist in properly setting up additional loadouts.      Scrapping Cards  Attempting to scrap a card used by multiple loadouts will display a message warning you that the card will be removed from all loadouts. If confirmed, the card will be scrapped and removed from all loadouts.

items.name: Sprinting
items.desc: Press [Sprint] to sprint.    Sprinting consumes Action Points (AP). If you run out of AP, you'll be unable to sprint.     You can slow the rate at which sprinting drains your AP by increasing your Endurance attribute.

items.name: Stash Box
items.desc: A Stash Box is a special container that safely stores any items you put in it.    Items stored in a Stash Box are accessible from any other Stash Box in the world. Typically, Stash Boxes are built by you at your C.A.M.P., but they can also be found in the world. The Train Stations and Red Rocket stations scattered throughout Appalachia each have a Stash Box.    Each Player can only see their own items in a Stash Box. So while multiple Players might be accessing the same Stash Box in the world, each Player is only seeing, storing, and taking their own items from it.    When crafting objects, any items in your Stash Box can be used for components. This is true for crafting stations and workbenches out in the world, in addition to ones you build at your C.A.M.P.

items.name: Terminals
items.desc: Access terminals to uncover useful information, unlock secure doors, take control of linked turrets, bots, and spotlights, or play holotapes.    To enter a terminal, approach it and press [Activate].     Navigate between terminal entries with [LeftStick]. Select an entry with [Accept].    To exit a terminal or terminal page, press [Cancel].      Hacking  Some terminals will be locked with a password. To hack a locked terminal, you must have enough "Hacker" perks equipped to match the skill level of the terminal.    If you fail your hack, you will be locked out of the terminal and can attempt to hack it again after 10 seconds.    For more information, see the "Hacking" entry.      Holotapes  Some terminals can hold holotapes. To eject or load a holotape, press [XButton].

items.name: Trading
items.desc: Trading between Players allows you to buy and sell items from each other for Caps.    Walk up to another Player and press [XButton] to invite them to trade. The other Player will need to look at you and also press [XButton] so that you're both in the Trade menu.    From the Trade menu, you can select items to sell and buy. The list on the left contains your inventory, the list on the right contains the other players inventory. Even if the item is not being offered, you can request to trade for it. You can filter the view to only show active offers by pressing [R3].    When you select an item to sell, you can set how many of that item that the other Player can buy. They will be able to purchase any number of that item up to the quantity you specify.     You will then be asked to set an Item Price. This is the price for each item the other Player purchases. For example, if you set the Item Price to 10, and the other Player buys 2 items, they will pay a total of 20 Caps.

items.name: V.A.T.S.
items.desc: The Vault-Tec Assisted Targeting System - or V.A.T.S. - allows you to hit nearby enemies based on a percentage chance instead of aiming.    To enter V.A.T.S., press [VATS]. To exit V.A.T.S., press [Cancel].      Attacking in V.A.T.S.  Press [PrimaryAttack] to attack the highlighted enemy. The number displayed on the enemy is your percentage chance to hit them.    You can switch between targets by pressing [QuickkeyLeft] and [QuickkeyRight].       Critical Hits  Every successful hit made in V.A.T.S. fills your Critical meter. Once full, you can press [ApplyCritical] and the next attack you unleash will be high-powered.    How quickly your Critical meter fills is determined by your Luck attribute.      Targeting Body Parts  Having 5 or more Perception will allow you to select specific body parts.    Use [Look] to select body parts on your current V.A.T.S. target. The bar below the percentage chance to hit number represents that body part's Health. Once the bar is empty, that body part will become crippled.    Weakness and Resistance  Having 10 or more Perception will allow you to see specific weakness and resistances of your target.

items.name: Vaults
items.desc: Vault Missions are challenging experiences intended for well-equipped, high-level teams. Preparation, communication, and coordination are essential for success.    Difficulty Ranks and Rewards  Vault Missions have difficulty ranks. Higher ranks offer greater challenges and greater rewards. The rewards for each rank are separate, and each may be earned once a day.    No Reentry  Once your team begins a Vault Mission, if you leave the Vault for any reason, you will not be able to get back in until the rest of your team has finished the mission.    Death and Respawning  When your Health drops to zero, no timer will begin. You can wait as long as necessary until someone on your team revives you. You can also choose to give up and respawn, but doing so will put you out of the Vault and off the mission.     Perks  The Wasteland Whisperer, Animal Friend, Robotics Expert, and Mysterious Savior Perks do not work in Vaults.

items.name: Vendors
items.desc: Vendors are typically robots that have been programmed by the previous survivors of Appalachia to sell goods.    When you find a Vendor, they will have a Trade prompt appear when you look at them. Press [XButton] to trade.    In the Trade menu, the list on the left contains your inventory, the list on the right contains all the items the Vendor has for sale. At the bottom of each list are the number of Caps you each have.    Select items in your inventory and press [Accept] in order to sell them. A Vendor that is out of Caps will not be able to purchase your items.    Select items in the Vendor's inventory and press [Accept] in order to buy them. You must have enough Caps to purchase the items, or the transaction will fail.

items.name: Workshops
items.desc: Workshops are locations in the world that you can temporarily claim and build on. Once you claim a Workshop, you get access to its store of building materials and access to the Workshop's rich resources.      Claiming a Workshop  Workshops are claimed by clearing its location of all enemy creatures, then activating the Workshop workbench and paying the Claim cost. A flag will start to rise, indicating your progress. If there are any Hostile Players in the area, they will contest your claim. Drive them out to continue claiming the Workshop.    Once claimed, you can activate the Workshop to start building. See the C.A.M.P. topic for more information on how to use the Building controls.    Your claim to a Workshop is temporary. Hostile Players who enter the location can contest your claim. You'll also lose your claim once you disconnect.      Workshop Resources  Every Workshop has resources you can extract by building Collector objects on them, and connecting the Collectors to power. Collectors are found in the Resources category of the Building menu. See the "Power" topic in the Help menu for more information about powering objects.    Collectors will add resources to their inventory over time until they are full, as long as they are operational. However, other Players can steal from a Collector's inventory, so build locks on your Collectors and Turrets to defend them.    Some Collectors can only be built on top of a "hardpoint," which is a specific spot in the Workshop area, such as an Aluminum Deposit or Gravel Pit. If a Collector is valid for that hardpoint, it will "snap" on top of it when you try to place it.    Each Workshop has different available resources, which are indicated on the map. Open the map and move the cursor over the Workshop location to see the list of resources with a number next to each resource. This is the maximum amount of each resource this Workshop will produce every "cycle."     For example, a Water value of 4 means that up to 4 Water Purifiers will produce each cycle. If you have more than 4 Water Purifiers, then the Workshop will randomly pick between the available Water Purifiers and produce at 4 of them. Water Purifiers that aren't powered or whose inventory are full are ignored, so if you had 6 Water Purifiers, but 3 of them were full, then the other 3 Water Purifiers would produce.
